features: THE ACCOUNT LEDGER (MASTRINO) — «All the bank movements» is the administrator's everyday question, and it had no answer: the Cash Book puts every cash account together and starts from zero each financial year, the General Ledger lists entries rather than accounts, the Balance Sheet gives a balance but not the lines behind it. Now every account has its own ledger: debit, credit and running balance line by line, over the period of the financial year in the bar. It sits under Movements as a child page of the Balance Sheet; a selector at the top switches account, grouped by type, with the number of movements in the period. The account name is the title, the internal code sits beside it, small.

THE BALANCE STARTS FROM THE BROUGHT-FORWARD, NOT FROM ZERO — The first line is what the account held the day before the financial year, including everything before it, previous years too; the last line is today's balance (or the end date, for a closed year), and it is the same figure as the Balance Sheet row you clicked from: the ledger is the detail of the snapshot and always closes on its number. The scope is by date: an entry dated outside its own financial year appears in the ledger of the period it falls in, with its year's badge. The balance is in the account's natural direction — debit minus credit for assets and costs, credit minus debit for liabilities and revenue — and turns red when against its nature: the bank below zero, a supplier in credit.

ONE CLICK ON THE ROW OPENS THE COUNTERPART — Under each movement the sibling lines of the entry appear, account, debit and credit: where the money comes from or goes to, even when more than one account is involved; with the recording date, the status, the note and a link to the double-entry record. The counterparty column uses the same sources as the Cash Book; on the receivables ledger every line carries its own unit owner, not the one on the adjacent line. Reversals as in the register: the original stays marked «reversed» — a reversed invoice too — and the reversal is a line like any other.

WHAT IT DECLARES INSTEAD OF HIDING — Above the table, when they occur: a cash opening balance not yet posted to the journal (the snapshot counts it, the ledger does not, and the difference is written with a link to the General Ledger); lines from other financial years within the period; lines of this year dated before its start, which sit in the brought-forward; movements dated after the end of the period. A financial year not yet started has an empty period and a brought-forward equal to today's snapshot, and the page says so. «Today» is the user's day in Italy, even at 00:30.

FILTERS THAT DO NOT INVENT BALANCES — Search on description, reference and counterparty; a date range within the period, and a date outside the period is ignored rather than producing a balance that does not exist. When filtering, the debit and credit totals become partial and say so; the balance at the date stays the true one, and the brought-forward is never filtered. A filter with no result is distinguished from an account with no movements.

THE PRINT, AND THE GENERAL LEDGER BOOK — An account ledger downloads as «mastrino-<code>-<building>-2026.pdf», landscape, with brought-forward, lines, totals and closing balance; with an active filter the sheet declares itself a «partial extract». From the «Print» menu, in the ledger and in the Balance Sheet, there is «All accounts — ledger book»: a single file with the ledger of every account with movements, one account per page, with an index on the cover, no filters. Same letterhead as the other three prints, unsigned: it is a computed register, not a deed.

THREE DOORS, AND YOU GO BACK WHERE YOU CAME FROM — In the Balance Sheet every account of the financial position and every cash account of the cash summary links to its ledger, at the same date. In Resources and funds the «Movements» action on the cash account row. In the General Ledger, opening an entry, every account in the detail leads to its ledger. The button at the top returns to the page you came from. The per-expense-item modal of the Chart of accounts stays as it is, and says so: it has its own scope rule (it excludes disputed invoices) and unifying it with the ledger is a decision for when that view is built.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE CASH BOOK AND TO THE .25 STORY — The «Only money that really moves» card and the note at the bottom of the print said the register balance «is net of the funds set aside». It is not: a transfer to a fund made by internal transfer does not appear in the register, so the bank line keeps counting it, like the bank does. The real reasons it does not match the bank statement are others: the balance is a single one across all real cash accounts and starts from zero each year; for the comparison, the cash account balance in the Balance Sheet applies, which includes the brought-forward. And in the beta.25 changelog the out-of-period entries of the trial were eleven, not twelve.

GUARDS — An account of another building, or a parent account with children, does not open from here: 404. Nineteen tests with hand-calculated expected values — brought-forward from a previous year, liability account against its nature, original + reversal, line from another year, opening not posted, filter with partial totals and true balance, post-dated line, future year, date boundaries in MySQL format, night-time in UTC, the ledger book — and the Cash Book suite stays green without touching a test.
